card.name: Lam Vong
card.tagline: Laos's graceful national circle dance of never-touching couples
card.profile: Lam Vong ('circle dance') is the national folk dance of Laos and the most popular social dance among ethnic Lao in Laos and Thailand's Isan region (Wikipedia: Dance and theatre of Laos). Couples move slowly counter-clockwise in concentric circles - men forming an inner ring, women an outer - never touching, using codified hand and finger gestures to the rhythm of the khaen; each cycle has eight movements repeated for the song's length (UNESCO ICH). UNESCO officially inscribed 'Fonelamvonglao' on 5 December 2024 at the 19th session (19.COM) in Asuncion, Paraguay (Lao News Agency KPL).
card.insight: Although emblematic of Lao identity, Lam Vong belongs to a regional family of circle dances shared with Cambodia's Romvong and Thailand's Ramwong - all transliterations of the same Khmer-rooted term meaning 'dance in a circle' (Wikipedia: Romvong).
